messages:
Alex (CSM): heads-up — Aurora Therapeutics onboarding: staging latency and cost warnings. p50 for small assistant completions jumped from ~110ms -> ~260ms over the last 24h. Token spend trending +22% vs expected. Renewal in ~6 weeks, want low-effort perf moves we can push before pilot expands.
Alex (CSM): quick list: 1) quantization options 2) model swap for cheaper tail latency 3) routing policy for burst isolation. Any quick, safe recs we can ship this week?
Raj (Solutions Eng): +1. From logs I see a lot of short prompt churn (avg input tokens 18). Good candidate for int8 quantization and aggressive prefix caching. Low risk if we keep a canary route.
Raj (Solutions Eng): immediate suggestion: try redwood/fast-3b-int8 (recommended profile) for non-sensitive routes. Expect ~30-40% token cost reduction and p50 improvement for short calls.
Priya (ML Eng): Agree. Also: set routing policy to split write-heavy vs read-heavy endpoints so dedicated pool handles bursts and hosted handles steady control traffic. Example policy snippet we use:

```json
{"routes": [{"name":"burst-dedicated","match":"request.tokens>100 || request.user_tier==\"enterprise\"","target":"dedicated-pool-aurora"},{"name":"default-hosted","match":"true","target":"hosted-fast-3b-int8"}]}
```

Priya (ML Eng): For safety, enable canary for 10% traffic for 48h, monitor hallucination/regression metrics (we'll attach a small prompt set).
Dana (AE): I'll coordinate the canary window with the customer. Can we give clear rollback instructions?
Raj (Solutions Eng): rollback = route traffic back to redwood/standard-3b (no quant) + disable caching changes. I'll prepare a rollback runbook in the ticket.
Alex (CSM): Great. Also, customer asked about impact on embedding accuracy — Aurora uses embeddings for rerank. Will int8 hurt that?
Priya (ML Eng): embeddings: avoid quantizing embedding model for now. Route embeddings calls to hosted-embedding-1. Keep generation quantized only.
Priya (ML Eng): TL;DR: model swap for generation to fast-3b-int8, routing policy to send heavy bursts to Dedicated pool, embeddings stay on hosted. Canary 10% -> 48h -> check quality metrics.
Alex (CSM): Cool. Any quick config we can give Aurora so they can opt-in via their config UI?
Raj (Solutions Eng): Paste this snippet (they can add as a route in their org settings):

```yml
routes:
  - id: aurora-canary-gen
    match: 'request.route_category == "assist"'
    target: redwood/fast-3b-int8
    percent: 10
    fallback: redwood/standard-3b
  - id: aurora-dedicated-burst
    match: 'request.tokens > 200'
    target: dedicated://aurora-pool
```

Raj (Solutions Eng): We'll monitor p50/p95, token cost delta, and embeddings drift via the eval set.
Dana (AE): I'll schedule a 30-min enablement call tomorrow 10am PT with Aurora CSM + infra lead.
Alex (CSM): I'll add the eval prompt set and baseline metrics to the ticket. 
ops-bot: Deploy triggered: routing-change-canary -> staging (initiated by Raj). :rocket:
Priya (ML Eng): quick note — watch KV cache hit rate. If hit rate low, caching won't help; fallback plan: reduce model to fast-1.4b for non-critical traffic.
Alex (CSM): thanks team. Will capture customer feedback after canary and prep renewal playbook if metrics improve. :thumbsup:
Dana (AE): +1, will loop legal for the upcoming contract conversation if numbers look good.
Raj (Solutions Eng): I'll post a short checklist in the ticket: 1) enable canary 2) monitor evals 3) confirm embeddings route 4) rollback script ready.
Alex (CSM): perfect. Closing thread for now — please update ticket with timestamps of canary start/stop and any anomalies.
